# Patterns in nature — Menges corpus (material computation)

**Card 11d · source workbook `ontology/xlsx/Patterns_in_Nature_Ontology_v3.xlsx` · generated by `scripts/build-knowledge.js` — do not edit by hand.**

## Scope boundary

Biomimicry where the material itself does the computing: fibre orientation, anisotropy, hygroscopic actuation, differentiated growth and computational fabrication. Strongest where the answer is a material system that responds without sensors or actuators. Complements 11c, which works at building scale with conventional systems. The base ontology is card 11a.

## Maturity guide

- **Level or note** — What it means here
- **Why this sheet exists** — The Menges corpus is unusual in biomimetic architecture: it contains several fully permitted, occupied, permanent buildings alongside research demonstrators. Collapsing the two would waste the corpus…
- **Research** — Peer-reviewed method or laboratory result with no built architectural demonstrator. Example: cross-sectional 4D printing.
- **Prototype** — Built at 1:1 as a temporary research structure, usually a student and researcher pavilion. No permit for permanent occupation, no thermal build-up, no fire or creep data. Most of the ICD/ITKE researc…
- **Design concept** — Published scheme with no realised version. Rare in this corpus — the institute builds almost everything it publishes.
- **Pilot** — Full-scale, publicly accessible, but in an exhibition or monitored research context rather than as a permitted occupied building. Examples: Elytra Filament Pavilion, Maison Fibre, Solar Gate.
- **Commercial / built** — Permitted building in permanent use, with a named approval route where a novel structure required one. Examples: Landesgartenschau Exhibition Hall, Urbach Tower, BUGA Wood and Fibre Pavilions, livMat…
- **What a maturity level does not mean** — A prototype in this corpus is often better engineered than a commercial product elsewhere. The level records regulatory and service status, not quality.
- **The permit question** — The single most useful discriminator. A permitted permanent building has survived proof engineers, an approval body, fire and structural review, and a real service life. BUGA Fibre is the clearest ca…
- **The bespoke machine question** — Almost every case here required a robotic platform that did not previously exist. Record this in Machine_Dependency. It is the most common reason a strategy that works at Stuttgart does not transfer…
- **The stock variability question** — For self-shaping work, prediction accuracy depends on whether the actual boards were sampled and sorted or simply specified. HygroShell sorted every board by grain angle and moisture. Record this in…
- **The baseline question** — Every performance factor in this corpus is stated against a named comparator. If a record has a ratio but no baseline, downgrade it rather than storing it.
- **The bio-based question** — A glass or carbon fibre result cannot support a sustainability claim. The flax and timber work exists precisely because the earlier composite results were fossil-based. Keep Material_Origin distinct…
- **Scale-up blockers seen in this corpus** — Bespoke robotic platforms; absence of design codes for novel joints and bindless structures; natural stock variability; fossil-based matrix resins in otherwise bio-based systems; design effort per un…
- **How to add a new record** — State the function first, then the biology. Record the mimicry level honestly — if only a shape was transferred, set Transfer_Verified to false. Name the baseline for any ratio. Give the permit statu…
- **Merging with the Pawlyn ontology** — All IDs in this file are prefixed distinctly (AM, MP, MM, MC, MR, ME, MS) so they never collide with the Pawlyn BA, BP, BM, CS, R, EV and SRC series. Add the Corpus field to both files before merging…
